data.body:
## S1 merged; its close failed on MY error, and the gate caught it

Change 2620 merged as bb65f47becfe 'Isolate review-gate scratch on its own EBS volume', carrying
rebar-ticket: aa40. Twelve changes merged tonight.

THE CLOSE FAILED, correctly: 'it records file_impact but no commit references it'. My error -- I ran
the close from S6'S worktree, not S1's. That worktree had diverged (it held S6's own commit), so my
'git merge --ff-only origin/main' FAILED, leaving HEAD eleven commits behind, and I chained the close
after it without checking the ff had succeeded. Fixed by resetting that worktree to origin/main (its
work is merged, nothing lost) and verifying reachability explicitly before retrying:
'git merge-base --is-ancestor bb65f47becfe HEAD' -> YES, and
'rebar verify-commit-ticket --rev bb65f47becfe' -> OK - resolved aa40.

That is the FOURTH time tonight I assumed a command's effect instead of verifying it -- after the
blind monitor, the patchset-base filter, and dispatching test.yml into a running job. Each time a gate
or a later check caught it rather than me. Worth stating plainly: the gates in this repo are doing
real work, and several of tonight's 'good catches' were catches of MY mistakes, not the tree's.

S1'S TWO SUBSTANTIVE FINDINGS, recorded on the ticket so a future simplifying edit cannot undo them:
 - REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR takes TWO env vars, not one. It moves the content-addressed store, but the
   review-bot's per-review clone is a plain tempfile.TemporaryDirectory following TMPDIR -- and that
   clone is the path whose bytes scale LINEARLY WITH CONCURRENCY. Setting only the first is half a fix.
 - An unmounted volume RAISES NOTHING. A mount point whose volume is absent is an ordinary, writable,
   EMPTY directory, so mkdir(parents=True) silently recreates the store on root and every gate keeps
   working on the disk the epic protects. S6's fail-closed-on-OSError cannot see it because there is
   no error. Hence two markers on two different filesystems: declaration on root (survives unmount),
   proof on the volume (vanishes with it); only declaration-present + proof-absent refuses.

And patchset 2 fixed a perfect inversion in its own patchset 1: the recovery runbook said 'touch
<mount>/.gate-scratch-mounted', which while unmounted lands on ROOT and tells the guard the volume is
present. THE RECOVERY PROCEDURE FOR THE SILENT FALLBACK WOULD HAVE PERFORMED THE SILENT FALLBACK.

FILED 1ef8-c849-5801-4eee (fillable-starry-aruanas, p1): the refusal guards gate_admission(), which
the review-bot clone path does not pass through -- so on a declared-but-unmounted volume the gates
refuse loudly while the review-bot clones onto root quietly. A PARTIAL refusal is arguably worse than
none, because the loud half creates confidence the protection is in force. Needs ADR 0069
retryable-deferral so it never becomes a false LLM-Review -1 against an innocent change.
